---
title: "Typography"
description: "Pick a typeface for scientific writing that works in print and on screen, preview it as a web page or a book page, and export the CSS and LaTeX."
toc: true
toc-title: "On this page"
show-reading-time: false
---

There is no single font that science agreed on, but there is a small family of typefaces designed for exactly this job. They carry a real italic, a full set of Greek letters and math symbols, tabular figures that line up in a table, and a matching math font so equations and prose share one voice. Most of them were drawn to survive both cheap paper and low resolution screens, which is what makes them usable in a book and in a browser without switching. This tool lets you audition those typefaces, measure how they behave, and see the result on a real page. The specimen renders as a printed page at real trim size, including approximations of the IEEE Xplore, MDPI, and ScienceDirect layouts, or as a plain web article once you switch the page view off. One button restyles this page with your choice, sidebars and navigation bar included, and another carries it to every page of the site. The settings export as CSS variables and as a LaTeX preamble.

```{=html}
    <div class="ty-h1">Measurement and Uncertainty</div>
    <div class="ty-h2">3.2 Propagating error through a nonlinear model</div>
    <p>A measurement without a stated uncertainty is not a measurement. When a quantity is computed from several inputs, each carrying an error of its own, the uncertainty of the result follows from the partial derivatives of the model with respect to every input. For small and independent errors the familiar rule in quadrature applies, and the terms that dominate the sum are the ones worth improving in the next round of the experiment.</p>
    <p class="ty-cont">In practice the estimate is only as honest as the assumption of independence, which is why correlated instrument drift deserves a separate line in the error budget. The <span class="ty-sc">iso</span> guide calls these Type B contributions, and they are usually the hardest to defend.</p>
    <div class="ty-eq"><span class="ty-num">(3.4)</span>&#963;<sub><i>f</i></sub><sup>2</sup> = &#931;<sub><i>i</i></sub> ( &#8706;<i>f</i> / &#8706;<i>x</i><sub><i>i</i></sub> )<sup>2</sup> &#963;<sub><i>i</i></sub><sup>2</sup> + 2 &#931;<sub><i>i</i>&lt;<i>j</i></sub> &#961;<sub><i>ij</i></sub> &#963;<sub><i>i</i></sub> &#963;<sub><i>j</i></sub></div>
    <p>Over the full data set of <span class="ty-osf">1 048 576</span> recorded events, collected between <span class="ty-osf">1997</span> and <span class="ty-osf">2004</span>, the weighted mean settles at 3.14159 &#177; 0.00042, well inside the band predicted by the toy model.</p>
    <div class="ty-tbl">
      <div class="ty-tbl-row ty-tbl-head"><span>Run</span><span>Events</span><span>Mean E / GeV</span><span>&#963;</span></div>
      <div class="ty-tbl-row"><span>1997A</span><span>148 322</span><span>91.1876</span><span>0.0021</span></div>
      <div class="ty-tbl-row"><span>2001B</span><span>9 041</span><span>91.1834</span><span>0.0117</span></div>
      <div class="ty-tbl-row"><span>2004C</span><span>891 213</span><span>91.1881</span><span>0.0008</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="ty-cap">Table 3.1. Event yields and fitted resonance mass by run period.</div>
    <div class="ty-h3">Implementation</div>
    <p>The calculation is one line once the Jacobian is available, and the covariance term is a single matrix product.</p>
    <div class="ty-code">grad = jacobian(model, x0)          # shape (n,)
sigma = np.sqrt(grad @ cov @ grad.T)  # 1-sigma on f(x0)</div>
    <div class="ty-cap">Figure 3.2. Residuals after the linear drift correction, binned in 25 ms intervals.</div>
    <div class="ty-quote">The propagation formula is exact for linear functions and a first order approximation for everything else. Kendall and Stuart, <i>Advanced Theory of Statistics</i>, vol. 2, &#167;10.6.</div>
  </div>

      math: 'TeX Gyre Pagella Math', tex: 'tgpagella',
      fb: 'Palatino, "URW Palladio L", "TeX Gyre Pagella", P052, Georgia, serif',
      note: 'The face MDPI journals set their body text in. It is not a web font, so this entry uses the copy installed on your own machine and falls back to TeX Gyre Pagella or URW Palladio.' },

    /* ---- sans faces ---- */
    { n: 'Source Sans 3', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: 'sourcesanspro',
      note: 'Clear at caption and label sizes, which is where a sans usually appears in a scientific document.' },
    { n: 'IBM Plex Sans', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: 'IBM Plex Math', tex: 'plex-sans',
      note: 'The sans member of the Plex superfamily, neutral enough for figures and interfaces.' },
    { n: 'Inter', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'Drawn specifically for computer screens and interfaces, with a tall x-height and open apertures.' },
    { n: 'Lato', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: 'lato',
      note: 'Humanist sans with a slightly warm tone, a common default in thesis templates.' },
    { n: 'Public Sans', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'A neutral and accessibility focused sans from the United States Web Design System.' },
    { n: 'Fira Sans', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: 'Fira Math', tex: 'FiraSans',
      note: 'Drawn for Firefox OS, with matching mono and math companions.' },
    { n: 'Alegreya Sans', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: 'AlegreyaSans',

    { n: 'PT Sans', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: 'PTSans',
      note: 'Companion to PT Serif, with the same wide language coverage.' },
    { n: 'Libre Franklin', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'A Franklin Gothic revival, good for headings that need presence.' },
    { n: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'A Braille Institute design that pulls apart easily confused letterforms such as I, l, and 1.' },
    { n: 'Open Sans', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: 'opensans',
      note: 'Wide and open, a safe neutral choice for figure labels.' },
    { n: 'Noto Sans', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: 'noto-sans',
      note: 'Broadest script coverage of any open family.' },
    { n: 'Nunito', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'Rounded humanist sans. This site sets its headings in it by default.' },
    { n: 'Roboto', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: 'roboto',
      note: 'Compact grotesque, the default on Android and the matplotlib style of many talks.' },
    { n: 'Archivo', r: 'sans', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'A grotesque built for highlights and headlines rather than body text.' },

    /* ---- monospaced faces ---- */
    { n: 'Source Code Pro', r: 'mono', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: 'sourcecodepro',
      note: 'Wide and calm, and it sits comfortably next to Source Serif and Source Sans.' },
    { n: 'IBM Plex Mono', r: 'mono', ital: true, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: 'plex-mono',
      note: 'The mono cut of Plex, with a true italic that reads as code comments.' },
    { n: 'JetBrains Mono', r: 'mono', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'Taller lowercase and a large x-height, drawn to be read for hours in an editor.' },
    { n: 'Roboto Mono', r: 'mono', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'Narrow and neutral, useful when code lines are long.' },
    { n: 'Fira Code', r: 'mono', ital: false, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: 'FiraMono',
      note: 'Fira Mono with programming ligatures, which look sharp on screen and odd in a printed listing.' },
    { n: 'Inconsolata', r: 'mono', ital: false, use: 'Print first', math: '', tex: 'inconsolata',
      note: 'Narrow enough that long code lines still fit inside a book measure.' },
    { n: 'Noto Sans Mono', r: 'mono', ital: false, use: 'Print and screen', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'Monospaced companion to Noto, with the same very wide glyph coverage.' },
    { n: 'Space Mono', r: 'mono', ital: true, use: 'Screen first', math: '', tex: '',
      note: 'Quirky and display oriented. Good for a title or a terminal, not for long listings.' },
    { n: 'System monospace', r: 'mono', local: true, sys: true, ital: false, use: 'Print and screen',
      math: '', tex: '',
      fb: 'SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace',
      note: 'Whatever monospaced face the reader already has. This is what the site uses when nothing else is chosen, so no download is involved.' },
    { n: 'Cousine', r: 'mono', ital: true, use: 'Print first', math: '', tex: 'cousine',
      note: 'Metric compatible with Courier New, for templates that demand it.' }
  ];

  /* The three font themes the Aa button in the corner cycles through.
     They are listed first so the tool can open on whichever one the reader
     already has, instead of claiming a choice they never made. */
  var SITE_THEMES = [
    { id: 'default', label: 'Site default, Nunito over PT Sans', b: 'PT Sans', h: 'Nunito', m: 'System monospace' },
    { id: 'reader', label: 'Site reader, Inter over Literata', b: 'Literata', h: 'Inter', m: 'System monospace' },
    { id: 'garamond', label: 'Site Garamond', b: 'EB Garamond', h: 'EB Garamond', m: 'System monospace' }
  ];

  var PRESETS = [
    { label: 'Journal (STIX Two Text)', b: 'STIX Two Text', h: 'Source Sans 3', m: 'Source Code Pro' },
    { label: 'Charter (Charis SIL)', b: 'Charis SIL', h: 'Lato', m: 'JetBrains Mono' },
    { label: 'Adobe Source superfamily', b: 'Source Serif 4', h: 'Source Sans 3', m: 'Source Code Pro' },
    { label: 'IBM Plex superfamily', b: 'IBM Plex Serif', h: 'IBM Plex Sans', m: 'IBM Plex Mono' },
    { label: 'Screen reading', b: 'Literata', h: 'Inter', m: 'JetBrains Mono' },
    { label: 'Classic book', b: 'EB Garamond', h: 'Libre Franklin', m: 'Inconsolata' },
    { label: 'Textbook', b: 'Libre Baskerville', h: 'Source Sans 3', m: 'Roboto Mono' },
    { label: 'Scholarly and multilingual', b: 'Gentium Book Plus', h: 'PT Sans', m: 'Inconsolata' },
    { label: 'Literary', b: 'Alegreya', h: 'Alegreya Sans', m: 'Fira Code' }
  ];

  var TRIMS = [
    { label: '6 x 9 in, US trade', w: 6, h: 9 },
    { label: '5.5 x 8.5 in, digest', w: 5.5, h: 8.5 },
    { label: 'A5, 148 x 210 mm', w: 5.827, h: 8.268 },
    { label: 'B5, 176 x 250 mm', w: 6.929, h: 9.843 },
    { label: '7 x 10 in, technical', w: 7, h: 10 },
    { label: '8.5 x 11 in, US letter', w: 8.5, h: 11 }
  ];

  /* Journal templates. The geometry is measured off published pages and
     the class files, close enough to judge a typeface against, but these
     are approximations rather than the official templates. Always start
     from the publisher files for a real submission. */
  var TEMPLATES = [
    { id: 'ieee', label: 'IEEE Xplore, two column',
      w: 8.5, h: 11, mg: { top: 0.75, bottom: 1.0, inner: 0.625, outer: 0.625 },
      cols: 2, gutter: 0.25, pt: 10, lead: 1.2,
      body: 'Tinos', head: 'Tinos', mono: 'Cousine',
      cls: '\\documentclass[10pt,journal]{IEEEtran}',
      note: 'US Letter, two columns of 3.5 in with a 0.25 in gutter, 10 pt Times throughout. Tinos stands in for Times New Roman here because it carries the same widths, so the line breaks match.' },
    { id: 'mdpi', label: 'MDPI, single column A4',
      w: 8.268, h: 11.693, mg: { top: 0.98, bottom: 0.98, inner: 0.98, outer: 0.98 },
      cols: 1, gutter: 0, pt: 9, lead: 1.3,
      body: 'Palatino Linotype', head: 'Palatino Linotype', mono: 'Cousine',
      cls: '\\documentclass[journal,article,submit,moreauthors]{Definitions/mdpi}',
      note: 'A4, a single wide column, 9 pt Palatino. The measure runs past 100 characters, which is why MDPI pages read dense. If Palatino is not installed on this machine the preview falls back to another serif.' },
    { id: 'elsevier', label: 'ScienceDirect, Elsevier two column',
      w: 8.268, h: 11.693, mg: { top: 0.98, bottom: 1.06, inner: 0.79, outer: 0.79 },
      cols: 2, gutter: 0.24, pt: 9.5, lead: 1.16,
      body: 'STIX Two Text', head: 'Source Sans 3', mono: 'Cousine',
      cls: '\\documentclass[final,5p,times,twocolumn]{elsarticle}',
      note: 'A4, two columns, around 9.5 pt. The elsarticle class defaults to Times, and the published face varies by journal, so STIX Two Text stands in as the closest freely available scientific serif.' }
  ];

  var TPL = {};
  TEMPLATES.forEach(function(t) { TPL[t.id] = t; });

  /* Glyphs a scientific text face has to carry before it is usable. */
  var PROBE = ['α', 'β', 'γ', 'θ', 'λ', 'μ', 'σ', 'φ',
               'Δ', 'Σ', 'Ω', '∂', '∫', '√', '∞',
               '≤', '≥', '≠', '≈', '±', '×', '÷',
               '→', '⇒', '∈', '∑', '∏', '²', '₀',
               'é', 'ř', 'ø', '†', '§'];

  var SAMPLE = 'A measurement without a stated uncertainty is not a measurement, and the ' +
               'uncertainty of a computed quantity follows from the partial derivatives ' +
               'of the model with respect to every input it depends on.';

  var state = {
    body: 'STIX Two Text',
    head: 'Source Sans 3',
    mono: 'Source Code Pro',
    size: 18,
    lead: 1.6,
    cpl: 66,
    ratio: 1.25,
    mode: 'screen',
    trim: 0,
    margin: 'even',
    cols: 1,
    pt: 10.5,
    tpl: '',
    theme: ''
  };

  var tool = document.querySelector('.ty-tool');
  var doc = $('ty-doc');
  var stage = $('ty-stage');
  var bookwrap = $('ty-bookwrap');
  var sheet = $('ty-sheet');
  var block = $('ty-block');

  /* ---- font loading ---- */

  var loaded = {};

  function byName(n) {
    for (var i = 0; i < FONTS.length; i++) if (FONTS[i].n === n) return FONTS[i];
    return null;
  }

  function fontUrl(f) {
    var fam = f.n.replace(/ /g, '+');
    var axis = f.ital ? ':ital,wght@0,400;0,700;1,400' : ':wght@400;700';
    return 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=' + fam + axis + '&display=swap';
  }

  /* Returns a promise that settles once the family is actually usable.
     Waiting on the injected stylesheet matters, because document.fonts.load
     resolves immediately for a family whose @font-face rules have not been
     parsed yet, which would leave every measurement reading the fallback. */
  function ensureLoaded(name) {
    var f = byName(name);
    if (!f) return Promise.resolve();
    if (loaded[name]) return loaded[name];
    if (f.local) {
      loaded[name] = Promise.resolve();
      return loaded[name];
    }
    loaded[name] = new Promise(function(done) {
      var link = document.createElement('link');
      link.rel = 'stylesheet';
      link.href = fontUrl(f);
      link.addEventListener('load', done);
      link.addEventListener('error', done);
      document.head.appendChild(link);
      setTimeout(done, 5000);
    }).then(function() {
      if (!document.fonts || !document.fonts.load) return;
      return Promise.all([
        document.fonts.load('400 16px "' + name + '"'),
        document.fonts.load('700 16px "' + name + '"'),
        document.fonts.load('italic 400 16px "' + name + '"')
      ]).catch(function() {});
    });
    return loaded[name];
  }

  function stackFor(name) {
    var f = byName(name);
    if (f && f.sys) return f.fb;
    if (f && f.fb) return '"' + name + '", ' + f.fb;
    var fallback = !f ? 'serif' : (f.r === 'mono' ? 'ui-monospace, monospace' : (f.r === 'sans' ? 'system-ui, sans-serif' : 'Georgia, serif'));
    return '"' + name + '", ' + fallback;
  }

  /* ---- measuring ---- */

  var canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  var ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  var EM = 200;

  function metrics(name) {
    ctx.font = '400 ' + EM + 'px "' + name + '", serif';
    var mx = ctx.measureText('x');
    var mH = ctx.measureText('H');
    var mb = ctx.measureText('b');
    var mp = ctx.measureText('p');
    return {
      x: mx.actualBoundingBoxAscent / EM,
      cap: mH.actualBoundingBoxAscent / EM,
      asc: mb.actualBoundingBoxAscent / EM,
      desc: mp.actualBoundingBoxDescent / EM,
      avg: ctx.measureText(SAMPLE).width / SAMPLE.length / EM
    };
  }

  /* A glyph is present when swapping the fallback behind the family
     changes the advance width. Two different fallbacks make a false
     negative very unlikely. */
  /* True when the family is really in use rather than silently falling
     back. Without this check a font that failed to download would report
     every test glyph as missing, which reads as a verdict on the design
     instead of a network problem. */
  function fontAvailable(name) {
    var word = 'mmwiWQ0oO1lI';
    var probes = ['monospace', 'serif'];
    for (var i = 0; i < probes.length; i++) {
      ctx.font = EM + 'px ' + probes[i];
      var base = ctx.measureText(word).width;
      ctx.font = EM + 'px "' + name + '", ' + probes[i];
      if (Math.abs(ctx.measureText(word).width - base) > 0.5) return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  function hasGlyph(name, ch) {
    var probes = ['monospace', 'serif'];
    for (var i = 0; i < probes.length; i++) {
      ctx.font = EM + 'px ' + probes[i];
      var base = ctx.measureText(ch).width;
      ctx.font = EM + 'px "' + name + '", ' + probes[i];
      if (Math.abs(ctx.measureText(ch).width - base) > 0.4) return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  /* ---- rendering ---- */

  function scaleSteps(base) {
    var r = state.ratio;
    return {
      h1: base * Math.pow(r, 3),
      h2: base * Math.pow(r, 2),
      h3: base * r,
      body: base,
      small: base / r
    };
  }

  function applyFonts() {
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-body', stackFor(state.body));
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-head', stackFor(state.head));
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-mono', stackFor(state.mono));
    return Promise.all([
      ensureLoaded(state.body),
      ensureLoaded(state.head),
      ensureLoaded(state.mono)
    ]);
  }

  function marginsFor(t) {
    var w = t.w * 96, h = t.h * 96;
    if (state.margin === 'canon') {
      return { top: h / 9, bottom: 2 * h / 9, inner: w / 9, outer: 2 * w / 9 };
    }
    var m = state.margin === 'even' ? 0.75 * 96 : 96;
    return { top: m, bottom: m, inner: m, outer: m };
  }

  /* Page geometry in CSS pixels, from either a journal template or the
     manual trim and margin controls. */
  function geometry() {
    var t = TPL[state.tpl];
    if (t) {
      return {
        w: t.w * 96, h: t.h * 96,
        mg: { top: t.mg.top * 96, bottom: t.mg.bottom * 96, inner: t.mg.inner * 96, outer: t.mg.outer * 96 },
        cols: t.cols, gutter: t.gutter * 96
      };
    }
    var tr = TRIMS[state.trim];
    return {
      w: tr.w * 96, h: tr.h * 96,
      mg: marginsFor(tr),
      cols: state.cols, gutter: 0.25 * 96
    };
  }

  function layout() {
    var px = state.mode === 'book' ? state.pt * 96 / 72 : state.size;
    var m = metrics(state.body);
    var avgPx = m.avg * px;
    var steps = scaleSteps(px);

    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-size', px.toFixed(2) + 'px');
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-lead', String(state.lead));
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-h1', steps.h1.toFixed(2) + 'px');
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-h2', steps.h2.toFixed(2) + 'px');
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-h3', steps.h3.toFixed(2) + 'px');
    tool.style.setProperty('--ty-small', steps.small.toFixed(2) + 'px');

    var cpl, extra = [];

    if (state.mode === 'book') {
      var g = geometry();
      var textW = g.w - g.mg.inner - g.mg.outer;
      var textH = g.h - g.mg.top - g.mg.bottom;
      var colW = (textW - g.gutter * (g.cols - 1)) / g.cols;
      sheet.style.width = g.w + 'px';
      sheet.style.height = g.h + 'px';
      block.style.padding = g.mg.top + 'px ' + g.mg.outer + 'px ' + g.mg.bottom + 'px ' + g.mg.inner + 'px';
      block.style.columnCount = g.cols;
      block.style.columnGap = g.gutter + 'px';
      block.className = g.cols > 1 ? 'ty-block ty-cols' : 'ty-block';
      var avail = bookwrap.clientWidth - 36;
      var s = Math.min(1, avail / g.w);
      sheet.style.transform = 'scale(' + s + ')';
      bookwrap.style.height = (g.h * s + 36) + 'px';
      cpl = colW / avgPx;
      var lines = Math.floor(textH / (px * state.lead)) * g.cols;
      extra.push(['Page', (g.w / 96).toFixed(2) + ' x ' + (g.h / 96).toFixed(2) + ' in']);
      extra.push(['Text block', (textW / 96).toFixed(2) + ' x ' + (textH / 96).toFixed(2) + ' in']);
      if (g.cols > 1) extra.push(['Column width', (colW / 96).toFixed(2) + ' in']);
      extra.push(['Lines per page', String(lines)]);
      extra.push(['Words per page', String(Math.round(lines * cpl / 6.1))]);
      extra.push(['Shown at', Math.round(s * 100) + '%']);
    } else {
      var widthPx = state.cpl * avgPx;
      tool.style.setProperty('--ty-measure', widthPx.toFixed(0) + 'px');
      cpl = state.cpl;
    }

    renderChips(m, cpl, px, extra);
    renderVerdict(m, cpl);
    renderScale(steps);
    renderGlyphs();
    renderExports(px);
    if (applied) pushPageFonts();
  }

  function chip(value, label) {
    var d = document.createElement('div');
    d.className = 'ty-chip';
    var b = document.createElement('b');
    b.textContent = value;
    var s = document.createElement('span');
    s.textContent = label;
    d.appendChild(b);
    d.appendChild(s);
    return d;
  }

  function renderChips(m, cpl, px, extra) {
    var host = $('ty-chips');
    host.innerHTML = '';
    host.appendChild(chip(m.x.toFixed(3), 'x-height / em'));
    host.appendChild(chip(m.cap.toFixed(3), 'cap height / em'));
    host.appendChild(chip((m.x / m.cap).toFixed(2), 'x-height / cap'));
    host.appendChild(chip(Math.round(cpl), 'characters per line'));
    host.appendChild(chip((px * state.lead).toFixed(1) + ' px', 'baseline to baseline'));
    if (state.mode === 'book') host.appendChild(chip(state.pt.toFixed(1) + ' pt', 'type size'));
    for (var i = 0; i < extra.length; i++) host.appendChild(chip(extra[i][1], extra[i][0]));
  }

  function renderVerdict(m, cpl) {
    var parts = [];
    if (m.x >= 0.5) parts.push('A tall x-height of ' + m.x.toFixed(2) + ' em keeps this face readable on screen at small sizes.');
    else if (m.x >= 0.45) parts.push('An x-height of ' + m.x.toFixed(2) + ' em is moderate, which suits print and asks for a point size on the larger side on screen.');
    else parts.push('A small x-height of ' + m.x.toFixed(2) + ' em is a book proportion. Set it a point or two larger than usual for screen reading.');

    var c = Math.round(cpl);
    if (c < 45) parts.push('At ' + c + ' characters per line the measure is narrow, so the eye returns too often and hyphenation gets ugly.');
    else if (c <= 75) parts.push('At ' + c + ' characters per line the measure sits in the comfortable 45 to 75 range.');
    else parts.push('At ' + c + ' characters per line the measure is wide, and the eye will start losing its place on the return sweep.');

    var minLead = cpl > 70 ? 1.55 : 1.4;
    /* A journal template carries the leading the publisher specified, so
       there is no point arguing with it here. */
    if (!state.tpl && state.lead < minLead) {
      parts.push('Consider opening the line height to at least ' + minLead.toFixed(2) + ' for a measure this wide.');
    }

    $('ty-verdict').textContent = parts.join(' ');
  }

  function renderScale(steps) {
    var host = $('ty-scale');
    host.innerHTML = '';
    var rows = [['H1', steps.h1], ['H2', steps.h2], ['H3', steps.h3], ['Body', steps.body], ['Caption', steps.small]];
    rows.forEach(function(r) {
      var d = document.createElement('div');
      d.style.fontSize = r[1].toFixed(2) + 'px';
      d.style.fontFamily = r[0] === 'Body' ? 'var(--ty-body)' : 'var(--ty-head)';
      d.textContent = r[0];
      var s = document.createElement('small');
      s.textContent = r[1].toFixed(1) + ' px / ' + (r[1] * 0.75).toFixed(1) + ' pt';
      d.appendChild(s);
      host.appendChild(d);
    });
  }

  /* Pulls the family name out of a stack such as '"PT Sans", sans-serif',
     which is how the controls read the page back. */
  function firstFamily(stack) {
    var m = /^\s*"?([^",]+)"?/.exec(stack || '');
    return m ? m[1].trim() : '';
  }

  function renderGlyphs() {
    var host = $('ty-glyphs');
    host.innerHTML = '';
    var live = fontAvailable(state.body);
    var missing = 0;
    PROBE.forEach(function(ch) {
      var d = document.createElement('div');
      d.className = 'ty-gly';
      d.style.fontFamily = stackFor(state.body);
      d.textContent = ch;
      if (live && !hasGlyph(state.body, ch)) {
        d.className += ' ty-miss';
        d.title = 'Not in the web font as served here, so the browser substitutes another face';
        missing++;
      }
      host.appendChild(d);
    });
    var label = document.createElement('div');
    label.className = 'ty-gly';
    label.style.border = 'none';
    label.style.fontSize = '13px';
    label.style.opacity = '0.8';
    if (!live) {
      label.textContent = state.body + ' is not available here, so the page is showing a fallback face and the glyph test is not meaningful.';
    } else {
      label.textContent = missing === 0
        ? 'All ' + PROBE.length + ' scientific test glyphs render from this font as it is served here.'
        : missing + ' of ' + PROBE.length + ' test glyphs are absent from the web font as it is served here, so the browser substitutes another face for them. Web fonts arrive as subsets, and the desktop or LaTeX release of the same family usually carries far more.';
    }
    host.appendChild(label);
  }

  /* ---- exports ---- */

  function importLine() {
    var names = [state.body, state.head, state.mono];
    var parts = [];
    names.forEach(function(n) {
      var f = byName(n);
      if (!f || f.local) return;
      parts.push(n.replace(/ /g, '+') + (f.ital ? ':ital,wght@0,400;0,700;1,400' : ':wght@400;700'));
    });
    if (!parts.length) return '';
    return '@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=' + parts.join('&family=') + '&display=swap");';
  }

  function renderExports(px) {
    var steps = scaleSteps(px);
    var lines = [];
    var imp = importLine();
    if (imp) { lines.push(imp); lines.push(''); }
    lines.push(':root {');
    lines.push('  --font-body: ' + stackFor(state.body) + ';');
    lines.push('  --font-heading: ' + stackFor(state.head) + ';');
    lines.push('  --font-mono: ' + stackFor(state.mono) + ';');
    lines.push('  --text-base: ' + px.toFixed(1) + 'px;');
    lines.push('  --leading: ' + state.lead.toFixed(2) + ';');
    lines.push('  --measure: ' + Math.round(state.cpl) + 'ch;');
    lines.push('  --scale-ratio: ' + state.ratio + ';');
    lines.push('  --text-h1: ' + steps.h1.toFixed(2) + 'px;');
    lines.push('  --text-h2: ' + steps.h2.toFixed(2) + 'px;');
    lines.push('  --text-h3: ' + steps.h3.toFixed(2) + 'px;');
    lines.push('  --text-small: ' + steps.small.toFixed(2) + 'px;');
    lines.push('}');
    lines.push('');
    lines.push('body {');
    lines.push('  font-family: var(--font-body);');
    lines.push('  font-size: var(--text-base);');
    lines.push('  line-height: var(--leading);');
    lines.push('}');
    lines.push('');
    lines.push('h1, h2, h3, h4 { font-family: var(--font-heading); line-height: 1.2; }');
    lines.push('h1 { font-size: var(--text-h1); }');
    lines.push('h2 { font-size: var(--text-h2); }');
    lines.push('h3 { font-size: var(--text-h3); }');
    lines.push('code, pre { font-family: var(--font-mono); }');
    lines.push('p { max-width: var(--measure); }');
    lines.push('table { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; }');
    $('ty-css').textContent = lines.join('\n');

    var fb = byName(state.body), fh = byName(state.head), fm = byName(state.mono);
    var tex = [];
    tex.push('% XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX, using the installed system fonts');
    tex.push('\\usepackage{fontspec}');
    tex.push('\\setmainfont{' + state.body + '}');
    tex.push('\\setsansfont{' + state.head + '}');
    tex.push('\\setmonofont{' + state.mono + '}');
    if (fb && fb.math && fb.math.indexOf('via') === -1) {
      tex.push('\\usepackage{unicode-math}');
      tex.push('\\setmathfont{' + fb.math + '}');
    } else {
      tex.push('% No matching Unicode math font for this text face.');
      tex.push('% \\usepackage{unicode-math}\\setmathfont{STIX Two Math}');
    }
    var pkgs = [];
    if (fb && fb.tex) pkgs.push(fb.tex);
    if (fh && fh.tex && pkgs.indexOf(fh.tex) === -1) pkgs.push(fh.tex);
    if (fm && fm.tex && pkgs.indexOf(fm.tex) === -1) pkgs.push(fm.tex);
    tex.push('');
    tex.push('% pdfLaTeX alternative, using the CTAN packages');
    if (pkgs.length) {
      pkgs.forEach(function(p) { tex.push('\\usepackage{' + p + '}'); });
    } else {
      tex.push('% None of the chosen faces ships a pdfLaTeX package.');
    }
    tex.push('');
    var tpl = TPL[state.tpl];
    if (tpl) {
      tex.push('% Journal class. Take the real template from the publisher,');
      tex.push('% since it sets the geometry, the headings, and the bibliography style.');
      tex.push(tpl.cls);
      tex.push('% Approximate geometry shown in the preview: ' + tpl.w.toFixed(2) + ' x ' + tpl.h.toFixed(2) + ' in, ' +
               tpl.cols + (tpl.cols > 1 ? ' columns, ' : ' column, ') + tpl.pt.toFixed(1) + ' pt');
    } else if (state.mode === 'book') {
      var g = geometry();
      tex.push('% Page geometry matching the preview');
      tex.push('\\usepackage[paperwidth=' + (g.w / 96).toFixed(3) + 'in,paperheight=' + (g.h / 96).toFixed(3) + 'in,');
      tex.push('  inner=' + (g.mg.inner / 96).toFixed(3) + 'in,outer=' + (g.mg.outer / 96).toFixed(3) + 'in,');
      tex.push('  top=' + (g.mg.top / 96).toFixed(3) + 'in,bottom=' + (g.mg.bottom / 96).toFixed(3) + 'in]{geometry}');
      if (g.cols > 1) tex.push('\\usepackage{multicol}  % or the twocolumn class option');
      tex.push('\\linespread{' + (state.lead / 1.2).toFixed(3) + '}  % ' + state.lead.toFixed(2) + ' of the type size');
      tex.push('% Body size ' + state.pt.toFixed(1) + ' pt');
    } else {
      tex.push('% Switch the preview to a book or journal page to get geometry values.');
    }
    $('ty-tex').textContent = tex.join('\n');
  }

  /* ---- catalog ---- */

  function renderCatalog() {
    var host = $('ty-cat');
    var filter = $('ty-filter').value;
    host.innerHTML = '';
    FONTS.forEach(function(f) {
      if (f.user) return;
      if (filter === 'math' && !f.math) return;
      if (filter !== 'all' && filter !== 'math' && f.r !== filter) return;
      var row = document.createElement('div');
      row.className = 'ty-cat-row';

      var name = document.createElement('span');
      name.className = 'ty-cat-name';
      name.textContent = f.n;
      name.title = 'Click to preview as the ' + (f.r === 'mono' ? 'code' : (f.r === 'sans' ? 'heading' : 'body')) + ' face';
      name.addEventListener('click', function() {
        if (f.r === 'mono') { state.mono = f.n; $('ty-mono-sel').value = f.n; }
        else if (f.r === 'sans') { state.head = f.n; $('ty-head-sel').value = f.n; }
        else { state.body = f.n; $('ty-body-sel').value = f.n; }
        refresh();
      });
      row.appendChild(name);

      var use = document.createElement('span');
      var tag = document.createElement('span');
      tag.className = 'ty-tag';
      tag.textContent = f.use;
      use.appendChild(tag);
      row.appendChild(use);

      var math = document.createElement('span');
      math.textContent = f.math || 'none';
      row.appendChild(math);

      var tex = document.createElement('span');
      tex.style.fontFamily = 'monospace';
      tex.style.fontSize = '12px';
      tex.textContent = f.tex || 'none';
      row.appendChild(tex);

      var note = document.createElement('span');
      note.textContent = f.note;
      row.appendChild(note);

      host.appendChild(row);
    });
  }

  /* ---- selects ---- */

  function fillSelect(sel, roles, value) {
    sel.innerHTML = '';
    var groups = {};
    var labels = { serif: 'Serif', sans: 'Sans', mono: 'Monospaced', local: 'Local fonts' };
    roles.forEach(function(r) {
      var g = document.createElement('optgroup');
      g.label = labels[r];
      groups[r] = g;
      sel.appendChild(g);
    });
    FONTS.forEach(function(f) {
      var key = f.user ? 'local' : f.r;
      if (!groups[key]) return;
      var o = document.createElement('option');
      o.value = f.n;
      o.textContent = f.n;
      groups[key].appendChild(o);
    });
    sel.value = value;
  }

  function fillAllSelects() {
    fillSelect($('ty-body-sel'), ['serif', 'sans', 'local'], state.body);
    fillSelect($('ty-head-sel'), ['sans', 'serif', 'local'], state.head);
    fillSelect($('ty-mono-sel'), ['mono', 'local'], state.mono);
  }

  /* ---- refresh ---- */

  var pending = false;
  var generation = 0;

  function refresh() {
    var mine = ++generation;
    var ready = applyFonts();
    if (!pending) {
      pending = true;
      requestAnimationFrame(function() { pending = false; layout(); });
    }
    /* Lay out again once the faces are in, unless a newer refresh has
       already taken over. */
    ready.then(function() {
      if (mine === generation) layout();
    });
  }

  function copyText(text, btn, done) {
    var restore = btn.textContent;
    var ok = function() {
      btn.textContent = done;
      setTimeout(function() { btn.textContent = restore; }, 900);
    };
    if (navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.writeText) {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(ok, ok);
    } else {
      var ta = document.createElement('textarea');
      ta.value = text;
      ta.style.position = 'fixed';
      ta.style.opacity = '0';
      document.body.appendChild(ta);
      ta.select();
      try { document.execCommand('copy'); } catch (e) {}
      document.body.removeChild(ta);
      ok();
    }
  }

  /* ---- events ---- */

  /* One list, two kinds of entry. A font pairing changes the three
     families and leaves the page geometry alone. A journal template also
     pins the page size, the margins, the columns, and the type size, and
     takes over the geometry controls while it is selected. */
  (function buildPresets() {
    var sel = $('ty-preset');

    var custom = document.createElement('option');
    custom.value = '';
    custom.disabled = true;
    custom.textContent = 'Custom';
    sel.appendChild(custom);

    var site = document.createElement('optgroup');
    site.label = 'Site font themes';
    SITE_THEMES.forEach(function(t) {
      var o = document.createElement('option');
      o.value = 's' + t.id;
      o.textContent = t.label;
      site.appendChild(o);
    });
    sel.appendChild(site);

    var pairs = document.createElement('optgroup');
    pairs.label = 'Font pairings';
    PRESETS.forEach(function(p, i) {
      var o = document.createElement('option');
      o.value = 'p' + i;
      o.textContent = p.label;
      pairs.appendChild(o);
    });
    sel.appendChild(pairs);

    var tpls = document.createElement('optgroup');
    tpls.label = 'Journal templates';
    TEMPLATES.forEach(function(t) {
      var o = document.createElement('option');
      o.value = 't' + t.id;
      o.textContent = t.label;
      tpls.appendChild(o);
    });
    sel.appendChild(tpls);
  })();

  TRIMS.forEach(function(t, i) {
    var o = document.createElement('option');
    o.value = String(i);
    o.textContent = t.label;
    $('ty-trim').appendChild(o);
  });

  /* The trim, margin, and column controls only make sense when nothing
     else owns the geometry. A template does, and leaving them on screen
     showing their old values would misreport the page being previewed. */
  function syncGeometryFields() {
    var show = state.mode === 'book' && !state.tpl;
    ['ty-trim-field', 'ty-margin-field', 'ty-cols-field'].forEach(function(k) {
      $(k).style.display = show ? '' : 'none';
    });
  }

  function setTemplate(id) {
    state.tpl = id;
    var t = TPL[id];
    var note = $('ty-tpl-note');
    if (t) {
      state.body = t.body;
      state.head = t.head;
      state.mono = t.mono;
      state.pt = t.pt;
      state.lead = t.lead;
      $('ty-body-sel').value = t.body;
      $('ty-head-sel').value = t.head;
      $('ty-mono-sel').value = t.mono;
      $('ty-lead').value = t.lead;
      $('ty-lead-val').textContent = t.lead.toFixed(2);
      note.textContent = t.note + ' The geometry here is a close approximation for judging a typeface, not the official template, so start from the publisher files for a real submission.';
      note.style.display = '';
      setMode('book');
    } else {
      note.style.display = 'none';
      syncGeometryFields();
      refresh();
    }
  }

  fillAllSelects();
  renderCatalog();

  /* Keeps the preset label truthful once the three typeface controls have
     been moved by hand, rather than leaving it naming a set it no longer
     describes. */
  function syncPresetSelect() {
    var sel = $('ty-preset');
    var i;
    for (i = 0; i < SITE_THEMES.length; i++) {
      var t = SITE_THEMES[i];
      if (t.b === state.body && t.h === state.head && t.m === state.mono) {
        sel.value = 's' + t.id;
        return;
      }
    }
    if (state.tpl) { sel.value = 't' + state.tpl; return; }
    for (i = 0; i < PRESETS.length; i++) {
      var p = PRESETS[i];
      if (p.b === state.body && p.h === state.head && p.m === state.mono) {
        sel.value = 'p' + i;
        return;
      }
    }
    sel.value = '';
  }

  function usePairing(p) {
    state.body = p.b;
    state.head = p.h;
    state.mono = p.m;
    $('ty-body-sel').value = p.b;
    $('ty-head-sel').value = p.h;
    $('ty-mono-sel').value = p.m;
  }

  $('ty-preset').addEventListener('change', function() {
    var v = this.value;
    if (v.charAt(0) === 't') {
      setTemplate(v.slice(1));
      return;
    }
    /* Moving to a plain pairing hands the geometry back to the controls,
       and keeps whichever view is open. */
    if (state.tpl) {
      state.tpl = '';
      $('ty-tpl-note').style.display = 'none';
      syncGeometryFields();
    }
    if (v.charAt(0) === 's') {

        if (SITE_THEMES[i].id === v.slice(1)) usePairing(SITE_THEMES[i]);

  $('ty-body-sel').addEventListener('change', function() { state.body = this.value; syncPresetSelect(); refresh(); });
  $('ty-head-sel').addEventListener('change', function() { state.head = this.value; syncPresetSelect(); refresh(); });
  $('ty-mono-sel').addEventListener('change', function() { state.mono = this.value; syncPresetSelect(); refresh(); });
  $('ty-filter').addEventListener('change', renderCatalog);

  $('ty-local').addEventListener('keydown', function(e) {
    if (e.key !== 'Enter') return;

  function bindRange(id, key, fmt) {
    var el = $(id);
    var out = $(id + '-val');
    el.addEventListener('input', function() {
      var v = parseFloat(this.value);
      if (key === 'size' && state.mode === 'book') state.pt = v; else state[key] = v;
      out.textContent = fmt(v);
      refresh();
    });
    out.textContent = fmt(parseFloat(el.value));
  }

  bindRange('ty-size', 'size', function(v) { return state.mode === 'book' ? v.toFixed(1) + ' pt' : v.toFixed(1) + ' px'; });
  bindRange('ty-lead', 'lead', function(v) { return v.toFixed(2); });
  bindRange('ty-cpl', 'cpl', function(v) { return Math.round(v) + ' char'; });

  $('ty-ratio').addEventListener('change', function() { state.ratio = parseFloat(this.value); refresh(); });
  $('ty-trim').addEventListener('change', function() { state.trim = parseInt(this.value, 10); refresh(); });
  $('ty-margin').addEventListener('change', function() { state.margin = this.value; refresh(); });
  $('ty-cols').addEventListener('change', function() { state.cols = parseInt(this.value, 10); refresh(); });

  function setMode(mode) {
    state.mode = mode;
    var sizeEl = $('ty-size');
    var book = mode === 'book';

    $('ty-tab-book').className = book ? 'ty-btn ty-on' : 'ty-btn';
    stage.style.display = book ? 'none' : '';
    bookwrap.style.display = book ? 'block' : 'none';
    (book ? block : stage).appendChild(doc);

    syncGeometryFields();
    $('ty-cpl').parentNode.style.display = book ? 'none' : '';

    if (book) {
      sizeEl.min = 7; sizeEl.max = 14; sizeEl.step = 0.25; sizeEl.value = state.pt;
      $('ty-size-val').textContent = state.pt.toFixed(1) + ' pt';
    } else {
      sizeEl.min = 13; sizeEl.max = 26; sizeEl.step = 0.5; sizeEl.value = state.size;
      $('ty-size-val').textContent = state.size.toFixed(1) + ' px';
    }
    refresh();
  }

  /* The book view is a toggle rather than a tab, because the screen
     preview is what the page shows the rest of the time. */
  $('ty-tab-book').addEventListener('click', function() {
    setMode(state.mode === 'book' ? 'screen' : 'book');
  });

  /* --- applying the choice to real chrome ---------------------------------
     theme-toggle.js owns the theme classes, the corner badges, the giscus
     theme, and the two storage keys, and it exposes window.siteChrome so

     the browser. Nothing is sent to Firebase or anywhere else. */

  var chrome = window.siteChrome || null;

  /* The families here are rarely among the ones styles.css imports, so the
     stylesheet links have to travel with the choice for other pages to be
     able to render it. */
  function fontConfig() {
    var links = [];
    [state.body, state.head, state.mono].forEach(function(n) {
      var f = byName(n);
      if (f && !f.local && links.indexOf(fontUrl(f)) === -1) links.push(fontUrl(f));
    });
    return {
      body: stackFor(state.body),
      heading: stackFor(state.head),
      mono: stackFor(state.mono),
      size: (state.size / 16).toFixed(3) + 'rem',
      lead: String(state.lead),
      links: links
    };
  }

  var applied = false;

  function setPageButton(on) {
    var btn = $('ty-apply');
    btn.className = on ? 'ty-btn ty-on' : 'ty-btn';
    btn.textContent = on ? 'Applied, click to undo' : 'Apply to this page';
  }

  function setSiteButton(on) {
    var btn = $('ty-apply-site');
    btn.className = on ? 'ty-btn ty-on' : 'ty-btn';
    btn.textContent = on ? 'Applied site-wide, click to undo' : 'Apply to the whole site';
  }

  function pushPageFonts() {
    if (chrome) chrome.applyCustomFont(fontConfig());
  }

  $('ty-theme').addEventListener('change', function() {
    state.theme = this.value;
    /* Preview only. The corner palette button still owns the saved value,
       which is how a reader gets back to their own theme. */
    if (chrome) chrome.setTheme(state.theme, false);
  });

  $('ty-apply').addEventListener('click', function() {
    applied = !applied;
    if (applied) pushPageFonts();
    else if (chrome) {
      /* Keep any site-wide choice, drop only what this page added. */
      chrome.clearCustomFont(false);
      chrome.applyCustomFont(chrome.readCustomFont());

  $('ty-apply-site').addEventListener('click', function() {
    if (!chrome) return;
    if (chrome.hasCustomFont()) {
      chrome.clearCustomFont(true);
      chrome.setTheme(chrome.getTheme(), true);
      applied = false;
      setPageButton(false);
      setSiteButton(false);
    } else {
      chrome.saveCustomFont(fontConfig());
      chrome.setTheme(state.theme, true);
      applied = true;
      setPageButton(true);
      setSiteButton(true);
    }

  $('ty-copy-css').addEventListener('click', function() { copyText($('ty-css').textContent, this, 'Copied'); });
  $('ty-copy-tex').addEventListener('click', function() { copyText($('ty-tex').textContent, this, 'Copied'); });

  var rt;
  window.addEventListener('resize', function() {
    clearTimeout(rt);
    rt = setTimeout(function() { if (state.mode === 'book') layout(); }, 150);
  });

  /* Open on what the reader already has. Everything is read back from the
     live custom properties, so the controls describe the page in front of
     them whether that comes from the site default, from one of the three
     font themes on the Aa button, or from a choice saved here earlier.
     Starting on some other typeface would make the whole panel disagree
     with the page around it. */
  function catalogName(family) {
    return family && byName(family) ? family : null;
  }

  function syncFromPage() {
    if (!chrome) return;
    state.theme = chrome.getTheme();
    $('ty-theme').value = state.theme;

    var cs = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
    var liveBody = catalogName(firstFamily(cs.getPropertyValue('--site-font-body')));
    var liveHead = catalogName(firstFamily(cs.getPropertyValue('--site-font-heading')));
    var monoVar = cs.getPropertyValue('--site-font-mono').trim();
    var liveMono = monoVar ? catalogName(firstFamily(monoVar)) : 'System monospace';

    if (liveHead) { state.head = liveHead; $('ty-head-sel').value = liveHead; }
    if (liveMono) { state.mono = liveMono; $('ty-mono-sel').value = liveMono; }
    if (!isNaN(liveSize)) {
      state.size = liveSize * 16;
      if (state.mode !== 'book') {
        $('ty-size').value = state.size;
        $('ty-size-val').textContent = state.size.toFixed(1) + ' px';
      }
    }
    if (!isNaN(liveLead)) {
      state.lead = liveLead;
      $('ty-lead').value = state.lead;
      $('ty-lead-val').textContent = state.lead.toFixed(2);

  }

  /* The two corner buttons can change the fonts and the theme out from
     under the panel, and the Aa button also throws away anything this tool
     applied. Re-read the page so the controls never describe a state that
     is no longer on screen. */
  document.addEventListener('sitechrome:change', function() {
    syncFromPage();
    refresh();
  });

  if (chrome) {
    /* This page is its own specimen, so the choice is live from the
       moment it loads. layout() keeps it in step with every control, and
       the button undoes it. */
    applied = true;
    syncFromPage();
  } else {
    $('ty-apply-site').style.display = 'none';
  }

  setMode('book');
  if (document.fonts && document.fonts.ready) document.fonts.ready.then(function() { layout(); });
})();
</script>
```

## What Makes a Typeface Scientific

No committee ever blessed one font for science, but the typefaces that survive in journals and technical books all clear the same short list of requirements.

The first is a **matching math font**. Prose set in one face and equations set in another produce a document where every formula looks pasted in from somewhere else. Only a handful of families solve this, because a math font has to carry the whole symbol repertoire plus the OpenType MATH table that tells the renderer how to stack fractions, size radicals, and grow delimiters. STIX Two Text with STIX Two Math is the clearest example, since the American Mathematical Society, the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, and the American Physical Society funded it precisely to solve this problem. Libertinus, Latin Modern, TeX Gyre Pagella, Erewhon, Fira, and IBM Plex all offer the same text and math pairing.

The second is **glyph coverage**. Scientific prose is full of Greek letters, comparison operators, arrows, degree signs, per mille marks, and accented author names in a bibliography. A face that lacks them forces the browser or the typesetter to substitute another font mid word, which is exactly the visual jump the glyph strip in the tool above exposes.

That strip needs one caveat. It reports what the browser can actually draw right now, and web fonts arrive as subsets rather than as the whole family. Google Fonts splits a family by writing system and sends only the parts a page needs, so STIX Two Text served over the web carries its Greek but not its mathematical operators, and Charis SIL arrives with neither. Both fonts hold the full repertoire in the files you install on a machine or load in LaTeX. The strip is therefore an honest answer for the screen half of the question, since a reader of your website sees exactly this, and it understates what the same typeface gives you in print.

The third is **figure handling**. Numbers in a table need to be tabular, meaning every digit occupies the same width so columns align without manual spacing. Numbers inside a sentence read better as old style figures, which have ascenders and descenders and sit in the text like lowercase letters. Good scientific faces ship both sets and switch between them through the `font-variant-numeric` property in CSS or the `\oldstylenums` and `\textfigures` commands in LaTeX.

The fourth is **a real italic and real small capitals**. Variables are italic by convention, and an italic that is merely the roman slanted by a slider looks wrong next to a proper one. Small capitals carry acronyms and running heads without shouting.

## Print and Screen Are Different Problems

A typeface for a book can afford fine hairlines, tight spacing, and a small x-height, because ink on paper resolves detail that a screen at 96 pixels per inch cannot. Garamond is glorious at 11 point on paper and thin and cramped in a browser at the same nominal size. A typeface for a screen leans the other way, with a taller x-height, more open counters, sturdier stems, and looser spacing, all of which look slightly overweight when printed.

The faces that work in both places were usually drawn under a constraint that forced the compromise. Charter was designed by Matthew Carter in 1987 for low resolution laser printers, so its sturdy, almost faceted forms happen to be exactly what a screen wants. Charis SIL is the freely licensed descendant of that design, and XCharter is its LaTeX counterpart. Source Serif, IBM Plex Serif, and STIX Two Text were all drawn in the era of retina displays and print on demand, with both targets in the brief.

The x-height to cap-height ratio in the tool is the quickest numeric proxy for this. A ratio near or above 0.72 signals a face that will hold up at small sizes on screen. A ratio near 0.62 signals a book face that wants a larger point size or a printed page.

## Measure, Leading, and Scale

Reading research and centuries of practice converge on a **measure**, the length of a line, somewhere between 45 and 75 characters, with roughly 66 as the classic target for a single column. Shorter lines force the eye to return too often. Longer lines make the return sweep unreliable, and the reader loses the row. The screen preview sets the column width from the actual average character width of the chosen face, so the character count stays honest when the typeface changes.

**Leading**, the distance from one baseline to the next, has to grow with the measure. A narrow column tolerates 1.3, a 66 character measure wants around 1.5, and a wide column needs 1.6 or more before the lines stop merging. Faces with a large x-height also need more leading than their nominal size suggests, because their lowercase letters fill more of the line.

The heading sizes come from a **modular scale**, a single ratio applied repeatedly to the body size. A major third of 1.25 gives a calm hierarchy suited to a technical document, while the golden ratio of 1.618 gives the dramatic contrast of a magazine. Using one ratio rather than hand picked sizes is what makes a set of headings look deliberate.

## Page Geometry for a Book

The book preview lays out a real trim size at real proportions, so the character count per line and the number of lines per page are the ones a printer would produce. A 6 by 9 inch page set at 10.5 point with three quarter inch margins lands near 66 characters per line in a face of normal width, which is one reason that trim size is so common for technical books. Larger trims such as 7 by 10 inch usually need either a larger type size or a two column layout, because a single column across a wide page runs far past a comfortable measure.

The third margin option follows the **Van de Graaf canon**, a reconstruction of the proportions used in medieval manuscripts and early printed books. It places the text block with an inner margin of one ninth of the page width, an outer margin of two ninths, a top margin of one ninth of the height, and a bottom margin of two ninths. The result pushes the text block up and toward the spine, which looks right once the pages are bound and which leaves room for the thumb. Notice that on a small trim the canon produces a measure well under 45 characters, since those proportions were worked out for pages much larger than a modern paperback. It comes into its own on the 7 by 10 inch and letter sizes.

## Journal Templates

The three journal templates set the page size, the margins, the column count, the type size, the leading, and the closest available typeface in one move, so a face can be judged inside the layout it will actually live in. A serif that looks generous in a 66 character web column has to prove itself again in a 55 character journal column at 9.5 point.

**IEEE Xplore** follows the IEEEtran class. US Letter, two columns of 3.5 inches with a quarter inch gutter, 10 point Times throughout including the headings. Tinos stands in for Times New Roman in the preview because it is metric compatible, meaning every glyph has the same width, so the line breaks fall in the same places.

**MDPI** uses A4 with a single wide column at 9 point, set in Palatino. The measure runs past 100 characters, which is far outside the comfortable range and is exactly why MDPI pages feel dense. Palatino is not a web font, so the preview borrows the copy installed on your machine and falls back to another serif when there is none. The free equivalents are TeX Gyre Pagella and URW Palladio.

**ScienceDirect** approximates the Elsevier two column layout on A4 at around 9.5 point. The `elsarticle` class defaults to Times, and the published face varies from journal to journal, so the preview uses STIX Two Text as the closest freely available scientific serif.

These are close approximations built for judging a typeface, not the official templates. The measurements come from published pages and class defaults, and publishers revise them. For a real submission, download the class files from the publisher, because they also carry the heading styles, the reference format, and the metadata macros that a submission is checked against. The LaTeX export names the right document class for each one.

## Seeing It as a Web Page

Chrome is where a typeface choice usually goes wrong. A face that reads beautifully in a 66 character column can fall apart in an 11 pixel sidebar link, and a heading face with tight spacing turns into mush in a navigation bar. This page carries the same docked sidebar and table of contents as the course notes for exactly that reason, so the two apply buttons give a real answer rather than a simulated one.

The controls always describe the page rather than themselves. The preset, the three typeface menus, and the size and leading are read back from the page when it loads, so if the `Aa` button in the corner has you on the reader theme, the tool opens on Inter over Literata and the preset says so. Pressing either corner button while you are here re-reads them again, so cycling the font themes walks the preset through them in step. Editing a typeface by hand moves the preset to Custom rather than leaving it naming a set it no longer describes.

**Apply to this page** is on from the moment the page loads, because this page is its own specimen. Everything around you, the navigation bar, the sidebar, the table of contents, and the paragraph you are reading now, is already set in the current choice, and it follows every control as you move it. The stylesheet of this site routes every family through four custom properties, `--site-font-body`, `--site-font-heading`, `--site-font-size`, and `--site-line-height`, so setting those on the root element changes all of that at once. Nothing is saved, so the effect ends when you leave. Click the button to drop back to the normal site fonts and compare.

**Apply to the whole site** carries the same choice to every other page. It remembers the font stacks, the two scale knobs, and the stylesheet links the families need, so the pages you visit next load them for themselves. The site theme selector switches the live page between the four color themes as it goes, since the same typeface carries differently on a white page and on a dark one, where thin strokes bloom and appear lighter than they measure. Applying site-wide saves the theme along with the fonts.

Everything is stored in the browser through `localStorage` and nowhere else. No part of the choice reaches Firebase or any other server, none of it appears in the page you share with someone, and it does not follow you to another browser or another device.

**Resetting** happens through the two round buttons in the bottom right corner, which are the permanent owners of these settings. The `Aa` button cycles the three built-in font themes, and picking any of them discards a custom choice. The palette button cycles the four color themes and puts the colors back. Clicking either apply button a second time also undoes it.

## Using the Export

The CSS block declares the whole system as custom properties, including the web font import line, so it can be dropped into a stylesheet and referenced from anywhere. The `--measure` value is given in `ch` units, which are relative to the width of the digit zero in the active font, so the column stays near the intended character count even if the font later changes.

The LaTeX block gives two routes. The `fontspec` route works with XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX and takes the fonts by name from the system, which is the simplest path when the fonts are installed. The package route works with pdfLaTeX and pulls the same designs from CTAN, where they have been packaged with the encodings and math support that pdfLaTeX needs. When the chosen text face has a matching Unicode math font, the export adds the `unicode-math` lines that bind the equations to the prose.
